Linear programming

Source: R/solvers-simplex.R
lpmin.Rd

lpmin(f, constr) and lpmax(f, constr) minimize and maximize the linear function f subject to the linear constraints constr (a list of non-strict inequalities and equalities) by the simplex method, as SymPy's functions of the same names; they return list(optimum, argopt) with the values of the symbols in a named list. Infeasible problems signal an InfeasibleLPError and unbounded ones an UnboundedLPError condition. linprog(c, A, b, A_eq, b_eq, bounds) minimizes c x subject to A x <= b, A_eq x = b_eq and the bounds (by default x >= 0) in matrix form, and show_linprog() returns the objective and constraints that linprog() would solve.

Usage

lpmin(f, constr)

lpmax(f, constr)

linprog(c, A = NULL, b = NULL, A_eq = NULL, b_eq = NULL, bounds = NULL)

show_linprog(c, A = NULL, b = NULL, A_eq = NULL, b_eq = NULL, bounds = NULL)

Arguments

f

The objective, linear in its symbols.

constr

A list of constraints.

c

Objective coefficients.

A, b

Inequality constraints A x <= b (lists of rows, vectors or matrices).

A_eq, b_eq

Equality constraints.

bounds

NULL, a pair list(lo, hi) for all variables, a list of pairs, or a named list of pairs keyed by 0 based index; NULL in a pair means no bound.

Value

A list of the optimum and the solution.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
lpmax(x - y, list(Le(x, y + 2), Ge(x, 0), Ge(y, 0)))
#> [[1]]
#> 2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$x
#> 2
#> 
#> [[2]]$y
#> 0
#> 
#> 
lpmin(x, list(Ge(y, 1), Ge(x, y)))
#> [[1]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$x
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]$y
#> 1
#> 
#> 
linprog(c(1, -1), list(c(1, 1)), 2, bounds = list(`1` = list(NULL, NULL)))
#> [[1]]
#> -2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> 0
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> 2
#> 
#>
